trust_decision.summary: lftest.test() decides whether a --test channel value is a file to read, using only os.path.isfile() with no containment, so any existing absolute or ../ path is read; separately, db_sqlite.get_db_path() decides the database location by joining an unvalidated filename onto the secured per-user directory.

landing_point.why: The advisory names lib.lftest and the live --test argument; test() is the only place a --test value becomes a file read (os.path.isfile() then disk.read_file()).

fix_sites.entry_point: lftest.test() - reached from every plugin's hidden --test CLI option (declared at args.py:108-112)
lftest._read_fixture(), called twice from lftest.test() for the stdout and stderr channels
db_sqlite.get_db_path() - public API also reached via connect() (db_sqlite.py:319), cache.get()/set() (cache.py:75, cache.py:149) and per_second_deltas() (db_sqlite.py:1030)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about lib.lftest and the hidden --test switch; get_db_path() is an unrelated SQLite path helper whose filename argument is supplied by our own plugin code rather than by the command line, so a solver can argue it is not part of this report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same value slot is legitimately inline stdout/stderr text when it is not a file (docstring: 'the string to be used as STDOUT'), and legitimate fixture values are relative subpaths under the plugin's unit-test/ dir (stdout/case, stderr/case); rejecting every value containing '/' or '..', or every value that is not a plain basename, breaks both. get_db_path() must likewise keep accepting ordinary names such as example.db and the default linuxfabrik-monitoring-plugins-sqlite.db (db_sqlite.py:749-750, tests/db_sqlite/unit-test/run:96-105).

O6_input_shapes: symlinked unit-test anchor directory pointing outside the tree
symlink below the anchor (unit-test/stdout -> outside directory)
relative fixture path inside the plugin's unit-test/ dir (stdout/case)
inline literal string that is not an existing file
the same shapes on the second (stderr) channel
database filename with a path separator, an absolute path, '.' or '..'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: import_csv(conn, filename, ...) opens a caller-supplied path directly (db_sqlite.py:878) with no containment; a base-dir + realpath containment check mirroring _read_fixture would be realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'caller-supplied filename is opened by a root plugin' pattern in the same module that just gained a filename guard; a maintainer hardening path handling would naturally guard this reader too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cache.get()/set() forward a caller-supplied filename straight to db_sqlite.connect() (cache.py:75, cache.py:149); a basename check or a dedicated cache path helper would duplicate the new get_db_path() guard at the cache layer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cache is the main consumer of connect(filename=...), so a maintainer could reasonably put the confinement there instead of, or in addition to, get_db_path().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: read_csv()/read_env() (disk.py:561-596) take a raw path and open() it; a base-dir confinement parameter would mirror the new _read_fixture containment.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These generic file helpers are where an engineer would centralise path containment, and the codebase already documents that get_tmpdir() callers must validate the final path themselves (disk.py:384-386).

O9_family: path traversal / arbitrary file read enabling local privilege escalation through sudoers-whitelisted plugins (CWE-22, CWE-269)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools/wheel via pyproject.toml [build-system] (pyproject.toml:1-5), pip; runtime deps in pyproject.toml:39-51; tests are plain python3 unittest scripts run per module
O10_build.project_tests: Per-module runners tests/<module>/unit-test/run driven by tools/run-unit-tests (tools/run-unit-tests:168-183); this area is covered by tests/lftest/unit-test/run (stdout/ and stderr/ fixture files) and tests/db_sqlite/unit-test/run - fast, fixture-based, stdlib-only, no network. Separate podman container tests exist elsewhere but do not cover this area.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Patch only lftest.test(): reject absolute paths or values containing '..' before disk.read_file(), ignoring symlinked anchors and leaving db_sqlite.get_db_path() untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The sudoers allowlist and the per-plugin --test argument splitting live in the consuming monitoring-plugins repository, which is outside this repository and was not examined.
Generic file helpers disk.read_file()/read_csv()/read_env() and db_sqlite.import_csv() open caller-supplied paths by design; noted as injection room only, not pursued as this advisory's flaw.
unverified: The advisory body itself was not available; only the candidate summary, the fix diff and CHANGELOG.md were read.
repo_mb (~2 MB) is estimated from source line counts (19,592 lines across 43 root modules plus tests), not measured; no shell access in this session.

Whether an attacker can reach db_sqlite.get_db_path()/connect() with a controlled filename depends on the consuming monitoring-plugins repo, which is out of scope; the advisory summary names only lib.lftest.
